name: Azerbaijan

facts.religion: Shia Islam about 65%, Sunni about 30%, largely secular

snapshot: Three years after retaking Karabakh, Ilham Aliyev is finalising a US-brokered peace with Armenia that includes a US-run transit route across Armenian territory.
culture: Azerbaijan is a secular, majority Shia country with Turkic language and close ties to Turkey. Mugham, an improvised classical music, is UNESCO-listed. Baku mixes a medieval walled city with oil-boom architecture like the Flame Towers. Novruz, the spring new year, is the major holiday, with bonfires and sweet pastries.
society: Oil and gas exports, including a pipeline to Europe, fund the state. Aliyev succeeded his father Heydar in 2003, and his wife is first vice-president. Independent journalists and activists are routinely jailed. The 2020 war and 2023 offensive returned Nagorno-Karabakh to Azerbaijan, and its ethnic Armenian population fled.
situation: For 30 years Azerbaijan and Armenia fought over Nagorno-Karabakh, a mountainous enclave inside Azerbaijan populated mostly by Armenians. Armenia won the first war in the 1990s; Azerbaijan, rich with Caspian oil and gas, won it back in 2020 and in 2023 seized the rest in a one-day offensive that drove out almost the entire Armenian population of about 100,000. Having won, President Ilham Aliyev, who inherited power from his father in 2003, has spent 2026 selling peace.

In August 2025, at the White House, the two countries initialled a peace agreement and agreed on the "Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity" (TRIPP): a US-run transit corridor through southern Armenia linking Azerbaijan to its exclave of Nakhchivan and on to Turkey, the route Baku had long demanded under the name Zangezur Corridor (CEPA). In 2026 the deal started to change facts on the ground. Aliyev declared that "peace has already been achieved" and that the two sides are "just learning to live in peace"; he lifted a ban on transit to Armenia, and from December 2025 Azerbaijani fuel began reaching Armenia by rail through Georgia (Carnegie Endowment). In August he wrote to Trump that relations had reached "their highest point in the 34-year history" (Eurasianet). The catch is a precondition: Baku will not sign the final treaty until Armenia rewrites its constitution to drop any claim to Karabakh, which Prime Minister Pashinyan plans to put to a referendum. TRIPP also cuts Russia out of a region it long policed, and Aliyev's relations with Moscow have soured badly.
power: A presidential republic in name, a hereditary autocracy in practice. The president has no term limits and appoints the vice president, his wife Mehriban Aliyeva, who would succeed him. Parliament is loyal, independent media have been crushed, and critics are routinely jailed.
